title: Selected Coupled Cluster Guided by Selected Configuration Interaction
abstract: Coupled Cluster (CC) theory is one of the most popular correlated wavefunction methods, yet the steep computational cost scaling of CC truncated at higher rank limits its application. Modern Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) methods successfully exploit the sparsity of ground-state wavefunctions in the determinant space, motivating an analogous approach with the exponential CC ansatz. In this work, we introduce Selected Coupled Cluster (SCC), an arbitrary-order sparse CC method that explicitly solves the CC residual equations within a compact amplitude space guided by an SCI wavefunction. SCC optimizes the CC amplitudes in the sparse amplitude space. Using a pilot Just-in-Time (JIT) compiled implementation, we benchmark SCC against SCI, SCI+PT2, standard rank-truncated dense CC (CCSD, CCSDT), and DMRG across various chemical systems. We demonstrate that SCC exhibits fast, monotonic convergence with the SCI variational threshold, outperforming SCI and surpassing SCI+PT2 in the tight-threshold regime. SCC also provides accurate energies for high-dimensional topologies, where DMRG typically converges slowly with bond dimension. SCC thus presents an efficient drop-in enhancement for modern SCI workflows.
summary: This paper presents Selected Coupled Cluster (SCC), a novel, sparse quantum chemistry method designed to overcome the computational limitations of high-rank Coupled Cluster theory. SCC leverages the sparsity inherent in Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) wavefunctions to guide the optimization of CC amplitudes. It demonstrates that SCC provides highly accurate and rapidly converging energy estimates, making it a powerful, drop-in enhancement for modern electronic structure calculations.
main_problem: The computational cost scaling of high-rank Coupled Cluster (CC) theory limits its application for accurate electronic structure calculations.
main_result: Selected Coupled Cluster (SCC) is introduced as an efficient, arbitrary-order sparse CC method that outperforms standard SCI and CCSD in the tight-threshold regime.
method: SCC solves the CC residual equations by optimizing amplitudes within a compact, sparse amplitude space guided by a modern Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) wavefunction.
model_or_system: The method applies to electronic structure problems governed by the time-independent Schrödinger Equation, using molecular systems like butane and circumcoronene as benchmarks.
key_observables: Energy (E), convergence rate, and the number of selected amplitudes required for convergence.
important_parameters: The SCI variational threshold ($\epsilon_{var}$), which guides the amplitude selection; the rank of the CC excitations (T).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the sparsity of the ground-state wavefunction can be effectively exploited by guiding the CC amplitude space using SCI methods.
figures_summary: Figures show the error in correlation energy relative to extrapolated DMRG energy for butane, and the relationship between SCC amplitude count and the SCI threshold for various systems.
paper_structure: The paper introduces SCC as an enhancement to SCI workflows, details the implementation using sparse data structures and JIT compilation, and benchmarks its performance against SCI, CCSD, CCSDT, and DMRG across several chemical systems.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum chemistry, the development of highly efficient, sparse, and systematic many-body wavefunction methods like SCC provides algorithmic insights applicable to simulating strongly correlated quantum materials.
